instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: The job is to repair tyre punctures on a Segway Xyber e-bike by patching the inner tube or plugging the tyre, ensuring the repair holds pressure after one hour. The critical safety aspect is preventing sudden tyre deflation in traffic, which requires scrapping tyres with sidewall or tread damage and verifying the repair by feel and spec pressure.

steps.title: Isolate Power and Disconnect Motor
steps.explanation: To prevent damage to the e-bike's electronics or accidental motor startup while removing the wheel.

fields.prompt: Confirm the motor cable is disconnected and electronics are powered off per the manual.
fields.guidance: Consult the Segway Xyber manual to safely disconnect the motor cable before removing the wheel.

steps.title: Inspect Tyre and Tube Damage
steps.explanation: To identify the puncture cause and ensure the tyre is not scrap due to sidewall or tread splits.

fields.prompt: Inspect the tyre casing for sidewall damage or split tread.
choices: Tyre casing is intact and safe to repair
Sidewall damage or split tread detected (Scrap tyre)
fields.acceptance_target: Tyre casing is intact and safe to repair
fields.guidance: Any sidewall damage or split tread means the tyre is scrap and must be replaced.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the debris or cause of the puncture.
fields.acceptance_description: The photo must clearly show the debris, nail, or thorn that caused the puncture.
fields.guidance: Capture a clear photo of the object causing the flat before removing it.

steps.title: Apply Patch or Plug
steps.explanation: To seal the puncture using a standard repair kit so it can hold riding pressure.

fields.prompt: Is the puncture hole small enough to safely seal with a standard patch or plug?
choices: Yes, hole is suitable for standard patch/plug
No, hole is too large (replace tube/tyre)
fields.acceptance_target: Yes, hole is suitable for standard patch/plug
fields.guidance: If the hole is too large for a standard patch to seal safely, replace the tube or tyre.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the completed patch or plug applied to the tube or tyre.
fields.acceptance_description: The photo must show the patch pressed down firmly and fully sealed over the puncture site.
fields.guidance: Ensure the area was roughed up and glue set before taking the photo of the applied patch.

steps.title: Reassemble and Inflate
steps.explanation: To return the tyre to its correct operating pressure as specified by the manufacturer.

fields.prompt: Inflate the tyre and record the pressure reading.
fields.guidance: Inflate the tyre to the exact pressure printed on the tyre sidewall.

steps.title: One-Hour Leak Test
steps.explanation: To verify the repair holds pressure over time and will not slow-leak in traffic.

fields.prompt: After letting the tyre sit for one hour, check if it has lost any air or gone soft.
choices: Tyre is firm and has not lost any air
Tyre has gone soft or lost air (repair failed)
fields.acceptance_target: Tyre is firm and has not lost any air
fields.guidance: Feel the tyre to ensure it remains fully firm. Any loss of air means the patch is no good.
